description: Deterministic manifest for the backend-only platform branch. Entries describe backend modules, backend operations assets, contracts, and SDK surface that may become a standalone backend repository.

entries.rationale: Headless reservation domain services, availability, capacity, conflicts, repository contracts, fixtures, and backend package examples are backend platform core.
Supabase storage adapter source is backend-owned and should move to the standalone adapter package after naming and compatibility cleanup.
Supabase adapter examples are backend adapter fixture candidates once current-app assumptions are removed.
The current Supabase adapter README should inform backend adapter documentation but needs platform-owned wording.

The existing Supabase adapter package manifest is copied into the materialized backend target candidate so the expected adapter package root has a concrete package.json placeholder until final package naming and visibility are reconciled.
The strict extracted backend build proof needs the Supabase adapter package TypeScript config alongside its package manifest and source until final package naming and build metadata are reconciled.

The strict extracted backend build proof needs the Supabase adapter package build TypeScript config alongside its package manifest and source until final package naming and build metadata are reconciled.

Package SQL assets remain backend-owned reconciliation/reference inputs for the database migration bundle, but the dry-run extraction plan must move the existing packages/database scaffold directly instead of copying these legacy SQL files into additional package paths.

The private backend-owned database package scaffold already exists in this repository with migration bundle targets, seeds, and ownership docs, so standalone backend extraction planning must include the package itself directly while the older root and adapter SQL assets remain reconciliation inputs only.
The backend-owned provider-neutral optional AI chat scaffold is an explicit standalone backend package candidate and must be represented directly in extraction planning.

The older reservation-chat-core package remains a current-app reference source for message/action/tool schema behavior that may inform the provider-neutral backend chat module, but it must not be planned as a verbatim copy onto the new ai-chat package target.
Shared API payload and error/idempotency types are backend platform contracts consumed by API, SDK, and external frontends.
The SDK is a typed consumer surface for the backend API and should ship from the backend platform repo while current frontend integration remains compatible.

Framework-neutral /v1 metadata, catalog read service/result mapping, repository ports, availability query preparation, reservation create validation/input preparation, reservation cancel validation/input preparation and response mapping, reservation reschedule validation/input preparation, reservation update policy mapping, resource-maintenance create policy, auth/context/idempotency/error helpers, and DTO mapping helpers are backend-owned package source.

The private standalone API skeleton is backend-owned source for optional Node HTTP hosting, framework-neutral /v1 route dispatch, injected repositories, service-token/JWT auth hooks, idempotency handling, and backend-only Supabase runtime dependency construction.
API resources, SDK methods, error conventions, and idempotency conventions define backend platform public contracts.

Backend repository bootstrap and backend package ownership docs are backend-owned operational guidance that should be materialized into the standalone backend candidate without copying frontend separation planning docs.

Reservation tables, RLS policies, atomic RPCs, and applicable security hardening remain Phase 5 reconciliation/reference inputs mapped by the SQL inventory and migration bundle manifests; the extraction dry run must not copy them verbatim into extra packages/database files.

Structured retrieval schema remains optional reconciliation/reference input mapped by the SQL inventory and migration bundle manifests; the extraction dry run must not copy these legacy SQL files into the package-owned database scaffold.
Local Supabase lifecycle helpers are backend operations candidates once environment names and current-app assumptions are generalized.

Generated backend root candidate source-boundary and database migration-index checks invoke these backend-owned scripts via node scripts/*.mjs. Monorepo-to-candidate extraction, package-graph, readiness, and migration-bundle reconciliation guardrails stay in the current repository instead of becoming post-extraction backend root scripts.

The generated backend root database migration-index check reads this repo-relative manifest by default. It must be materialized with the script so the candidate root command does not fail immediately on a missing default input file.
